title: Narrowband probe — daily grid (personal experiment tracker)
content:
Purpose: quick personal ledger for narrowband/batch experiments — keep small daily rows, notes and immediate next steps. Not meant for canonical logs; copy into the main benchboard when clean.

Layout (columns):
Date,RunID,BatchSize,Model,Quant,KV-cache? ,SeqLenAvg,TokensOut,AvgLat(ms),P95(ms),CostPer1k($),Throughput(tok/s),Notes,NextAction

CSV rows (most recent at top):
2025-02-14,nb-20250214-03,16,redwood-v2-7b,8-bit,yes,128,9.4k,42,94,0.012,220,"weird p95 spike around 13:02 — correlated with other runs; possible noisy host; verified no OOM. try isolate host next","re-run on dedicated node; add per-run trace"
2025-02-13,nb-20250213-11,8,redwood-v2-7b,4-bit,no,64,4.6k,29,57,0.009,160,"good steady; quality check (prompt clamping) looks OK; hallucination rate ~0.6% on tiny eval set","schedule 1k-sample eval overnight"
2025-02-12,nb-20250212-02,32,redwood-v2-13b,8-bit,yes,256,24.8k,88,210,0.031,280,"batching helps throughput but p95 goes high for long sequences; KV cache miss on warm-up","try prefix cache + warmup requests"
2025-01-28,nb-20250128-09,4,redwood-compat-7b,fp16,no,32,1.2k,18,39,0.006,90,"control run — baseline before quant experiments; low cost as expected","none"
2024-12-05,nb-20241205-01,64,redwood-v2-13b,quant-3,no,512,44k,320,790,0.082,540,"stress test; tokens/s degraded after 45s — probably memory thrash; check kernel logs","open INF ticket; capture dmesg next run"

Notes to self (quick):
- When p95 > 4x avg, suspect noisy scheduler or preemption. Check node metric: cpu steal / io wait.
- Always tag runID with host and queue type (dedicated|burst|shared) — forgot this twice.
- Keep a short eval prompt set (20 queries) to run after any quant change; helps flag quality regressions quickly.

Loose TODOs / followups:
- Add a tiny bash wrapper to upload JSON row to main benchboard: benchboard.upload --file row.json (blocked by PR #678 review).
- Investigate INF-2347 regressions — cross-check with Maya's trace from 2025-02-10.
- Try 6-bit LLMQ profile on 7b with batch size 12 (midpoint between 8/16) and measure p50/p95.

Scratch thoughts (riff):
- Could use a short rolling median window for p95 to smooth scheduler noise. But be careful, smoothing hides intermittent spikes which matter for tail SLOs.
- If we can detect warm-up pattern (first 3 tokens slower) we could emit an artificial prefix token in synthetic runs to warm caches — hacky but may reduce burst p95.

Quick reference: command snippets I used
- run (local): ./run_bench --model redwood-v2-7b --batch 16 --quant 8 --kv-cache
- export single-run csv: benchreport --run nb-20250214-03 --format csv > run.csv

End of sheet. (Personal; move to shared benchboard when stable.)
